movie.title: Resident Evil: Retribution
movie.overview: The Umbrella Corporation’s deadly T-virus continues to ravage the Earth, transforming the global population into legions of the flesh eating Undead. The human race’s last and only hope, Alice, awakens in the heart of Umbrella’s most clandestine operations facility and unveils more of her mysterious past as she delves further into the complex. Without a safe haven, Alice continues to hunt those responsible for the outbreak; a chase that takes her from Tokyo to New York, Washington, D.C. and Moscow, culminating in a mind-blowing revelation that will force her to rethink everything that she once thought to be true. Aided by new found allies and familiar friends, Alice must fight to survive long enough to escape a hostile world on the brink of oblivion. The countdown has begun.

reviews.author: Dark Jedi
reviews.content:
This movie is the 5th instalment in the Resident Evil series. Why would you want to watch this movie? Why would you want to watch any Resident Evil movie come to think about? Good acting…nope. Intelligent and intriguing plot…absolutely not. Zombies…yep. Action…most definitely yes! Anything else…well if you’re member of the younger part of the average male population you probably watch it for Milla Jovovich as well.

Now that we have established the baseline for the movie, does this movie deliver? The answer to that is, without a doubt, YES! This film delivered exactly what I expected of it. As I mentioned it is the 5th movie in the series and the entire series is sprung from a video game in the first place so it should really be no surprise that the film is one long video game action sequence sporadically interrupted with some dialog. Yet a lot of people seems to expect something else and judges the movie by those expectations.

I think those really low rating are quite unfair. The movie does indeed deliver what I think you should expect. A lot of the action scenes are marvellous. The slow motion scenes are well done and enjoyable unlike some movies where they are just annoying. The zombies and other monsters are good. And yes, I confess that, although I’m hardly among the younger part f the mail audience anymore I do like watching Milla Jovovich jumping around in the scenes in those ridiculous skin tight suits.

If I should complain about anything it would be that I sat through half the movie being annoyed that nobody would get the, painfully obvious, idea to rip that red mind control gizmo off Jill’s chest. When it was finally done in the end it was like “did you really have to take that long to get that idea into your head you dumb bastards”.

I cannot really give the movie a top rating since it does lack much of a story after all but I certainly think it is worth 7 out of 10 stars. I enjoyed myself a lot while watching it. The ending is the usual video-game-movie cliff-hanger and I really hope they make another sequel now when Alice got her powers back. That she lost those was one of the big downers for me in one of the previous movies in the franchise.

reviews.author: JPV852
reviews.content: Watching it again after 8 years, my feelings about this installment remains the same. Guess I found it easier to watch after revisiting the franchise but still think the plot was weak, even by the standards of the series, and while I know it’s based on a video game, really wish the movie didn’t feel like one, even more so than the previous installments. Still like Jovovich in the role of Alice, in fact, and take this for what you will, is the strongest actor of the ensemble with Guillory turning in an especially awful performance (at least under the Umbrella Corp’s influence). Easily this is the weakest entry. **1.5/5**

reviews.author: RalphRahal
reviews.content:
Resident Evil: Retribution (2012) is the point where the franchise fully embraces its identity as a straight-up action spectacle. Any remaining traces of horror are wiped away, making room for relentless fight sequences, wild set pieces, and high-energy pacing. The plot is simple and mostly exists to keep the action moving, but it does introduce some interesting elements, like Ada Wong’s arrival and the expanding influence of Umbrella. That said, while the story has potential, it never really dives deep into anything, keeping everything surface-level.

The directing sticks to Paul W.S. Anderson’s usual style, with slow-motion overload and CGI-heavy action. The cinematography, handled once again by Glen MacPherson, maintains the same hyper-stylized approach as the previous films, and while it looks slick, it can feel repetitive. Editing-wise, it is still messy, but at this point, it is almost a signature of the franchise. Despite its flaws, the movie has some fun sequences, and a few moments hit well, especially in terms of visual spectacle.

Milla Jovovich continues to be the glue holding everything together, bringing the same energy and badassery that keeps these movies watchable. She makes every action scene feel engaging, even when the script does not offer much in terms of depth or dialogue. The soundtrack keeps up the fast-paced, high-energy vibe, fitting the film’s style. While Retribution is far from perfect, and definitely not the best in the series, it is still enjoyable in its own chaotic way. If you go into it expecting pure action and nothing else, there is fun to be had, even if the franchise’s roots are long gone.

aiEnrichment.summary_one_sentence: Alice fights her way through Umbrella's underground simulation facility to escape and join the ultimate battle for humanity's survival.
aiEnrichment.summary_short: Awakening inside Umbrella's premier clandestine testing facility, Alice learns that the deadly T-virus has completely ravaged the globe. Joined by an unlikely strike team organized by her former nemesis, Ada Wong and Albert Wesker, she must navigate virtual simulations of major world cities infested with biological weapons. To reach the surface, Alice faces off against mind-controlled former allies in a relentless bid to save the remaining human race.
aiEnrichment.summary_long: Following the attack on the Arcadia, Alice is captured by the Umbrella Corporation and awakens in a high-tech facility deep within the Russian Arctic. She is freed from her cell by Ada Wong, who reveals that Albert Wesker organized her rescue because humanity needs Alice to survive. The facility operates massive, realistic simulations of cities like Tokyo, New York, and Moscow to showcase viral outbreaks to foreign buyers. As Alice and Ada navigate these deadly virtual environments, a rescue team led by Leon S. Kennedy moves inward to meet them. Standing in their way is a mind-controlled Jill Valentine, who commands a squad of familiar, cloned allies reprogrammed to terminate Alice. Throughout her escape, Alice protects a young clone named Becky, who believes Alice is her mother, adding a personal stake to her survival. After intense battles against giant Executioners, Lickers, and armed clones, the team manages to destroy the facility. Confronted on the ice by Jill and Rain, Alice manages to remove Jill's control scarab and defeat the upgraded super-clone of Rain. With the rescue team secured, Alice is brought to Washington, D.C., where Wesker restores her superhuman abilities to prepare for humanity's final stand.
aiEnrichment.synopsis: The Umbrella Corporation's deadly T-virus has swept across the globe, turning the vast majority of the human population into legions of flesh-eating Undead. Alice awakens inside the heart of Umbrella's most secret operations facility, where she unveils deeper mysteries about her past while attempting a perilous escape. Without a safe haven, she navigates simulated viral outbreaks modeled after major metropolitan hubs like Tokyo, New York, and Moscow. Aided by new allies, iconic operatives, and familiar faces, Alice must fight through waves of altered biological weapons and former friends turned enemies to reach the surface and prevent the complete extinction of mankind.

faq.answer: Yes, it is the fifth installment in the live-action Resident Evil film franchise, following Resident Evil: Afterlife (2010) and preceding Resident Evil: The Final Chapter (2016).
faq.question: Is Resident Evil: Retribution part of a movie franchise?

faq.answer: The dominant genres of the movie are action, horror, and science fiction.
faq.question: What is the dominant genre of Resident Evil: Retribution?

faq.answer: No, there is no mid-credits or post-credits scene in Resident Evil: Retribution, though the film ends with a dramatic cliffhanger leading directly into the next movie.
faq.question: Is there a post-credits scene in Resident Evil: Retribution?

faq.answer: Alice, played by Milla Jovovich, is the primary protagonist continuing her struggle against the Umbrella Corporation.
faq.question: Who is the main protagonist of the film?

faq.answer: Alice awakens inside a clandestine Umbrella Corporation testing facility and must fight her way out through simulated cityscapes while uncovering secrets about her past and fighting the T-virus outbreak.
faq.question: What is the primary storyline of Resident Evil: Retribution?

faq.answer: The underground Umbrella facility features simulated versions of Tokyo, New York, Washington, D.C., and Moscow.
faq.question: Which major global cities appear in the movie's simulated environments?

faq.answer: Yes, fan-favorite characters from the video games make their live-action debuts in this film, including Ada Wong, Leon S. Kennedy, and Barry Burton.
faq.question: Are popular characters from the video game franchise introduced in this movie?

faq.answer: The movie was written and directed by Paul W. S. Anderson, who directed several other entries in the Resident Evil film series.
faq.question: Who directed Resident Evil: Retribution?

faq.answer: The primary threat is the Umbrella Corporation's unleashed T-virus, which turns humans into flesh-eating Undead and creates aggressive bio-organic monsters.
faq.question: What is the main threat to humanity featured in the film?

faq.answer: Yes, the movie features returning characters and clones of past allies and enemies, including Jill Valentine, Carlos Olivera, Rain Ocampo, and Luther West.
